newsitem.title: UK: UK power firms warn on price proposals - report.
newsitem.headline: UK power firms warn on price proposals - report.

text.p: Britain's regional electricity companies have warned the government that proposed new price structures would wipe out supply profits, the Independent said on Thursday.

The newspaper said the Electricity Association, which represents power companies, wrote to Industry Minister John Battle two weeks ago claiming that the profit margin on supply, accounting for around seven percent of bills, would be so drastically cut that it would be uneconomic for any new operators to enter the market.

The domestic electricity market is due to be opened up to competition from April 1998 and Professor Stephen Littlechild, head of industry watchdog Offer, has issued a consultation paper on issues regarding liberalisation.
